name: Delta-beta-thalassemia

criteria.description: Presence of elevated HbF and reduced or absent HbA and HbA2 on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Identification of deletions or mutations in delta and beta globin genes by molecular genetic testing
Clinical features consistent with thalassemia including mild to moderate anemia and microcytosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic hemoglobin electrophoresis pattern plus confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be complicated by co-inheritance of other hemoglobinopathies

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with normal to elevated RBC count
Elevated HbF with absent or markedly reduced HbA and HbA2 on hemoglobin electrophoresis
imaging: Skull and facial bone X-rays showing marrow hyperplasia
Ultrasound evidence of splenomegaly and hepatomegaly
other: Elevated serum bilirubin due to hemolysis
Normal to mildly elevated serum ferritin unless transfused

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or mildly elevated HbA2 levels
Absence of delta globin gene deletion
Elevated HbF without anemia or microcytosis

redFlags: Signs of iron overload such as cardiac or endocrine dysfunction
references: Hoffman R, et al. Hematology: Basic Principles and Practice. 7th Edition. 2018.
Thein SL. Genetic modifiers of beta-thalassemia. Haematologica. 2013.
